fields.topic_name: Probability distributions, expectation, variance, covariance
fields.description:
Learning goal

Become comfortable with Probability distributions, expectation, variance, covariance as part of Statistics for quantitative research. Study common return distributions (normal, Student-t, empirical), moments, skew and kurtosis; estimate rolling covariance and explain fat tails. The purpose is not just to memorize terminology: you should be able to explain the underlying assumptions, implement a small example, and identify when the method produces misleading results.

What to study

  • Foundations: Define the important quantities, inputs, outputs, and assumptions behind probability distributions, expectation, variance, covariance. Write down at least one equation or concrete example in your own words.
  • Market context: Connect the topic to public daily price returns or simulated return series. Explain how distribution shape, sampling uncertainty, and the cost of false discoveries could affect the conclusion.
  • Failure modes: Check timestamps, missing observations, outliers, sample size, and inappropriate use of future information. Distinguish predictive association from a tradable, causal advantage.

Hands-on exercise

  1. Implement: Create histograms and Q-Q plots; compare normal versus Student-t tail frequencies.
  2. Evaluate: Establish a simple baseline, compare results on an appropriate later period, and record at least one metric plus uncertainty or sensitivity analysis. Use conceptual study and guided practice rather than copying unexplained example output.
